fact: Never delete existing tests — fix the code or the test instead
recommendation: If a test seems wrong, explain to the user and get approval before removing

fact: Do not cd into landing/ and run bun/vite manually
recommendation: Always use ./scripts/landing-start.sh for the landing page

fact: Launching pytest / npm test / long eval scripts / one-shot dev-servers via run_in_background=true without a planned reap
recommendation: Foreground + Bash timeout parameter is the safe default. If background is required, the launching turn must also plan: BashOutput follow-up + explicit KillShell before context loss.

fact: Using a self-reviewing agent loop's 'review found nothing' as the stop condition for an automated pipeline
recommendation: When user wants /spec-writer → /council-plan → /council-implement → /council-review on loop, do not let council-review be the sole exit gate. Same-model implement→review converges on 'looks good' by iter 2-3 via confirmation bias. Wire objective gates instead: typecheck pass + tests pass + coverage ≥ threshold + max-iteration cap (e.g. 5). Council-review tells the loop WHAT to fix; gates tell it WHETHER to stop. If feasible, spawn the review pass in a fresh sub-agent without implementation context.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 user asked about full auto-loop feasibility; flagged confirmation-bias risk as the main tradeoff

fact: A gate that can only fail is the same defect as a gate that can only pass — both teach the operator to ignore it
recommendation: When adding a canary, probe BOTH directions: mutate the tree so it must fail, and confirm it passes on a clean tree AND on legitimate variation. Two real instances in the council catalog: the pre-dispatch placeholder assertion fired on 49/59 phase files that legitimately retain output-template brackets (could only fail), and C11's 0755 directory FLOOR rejected a strictly safer 0750 (punished hardening). A gate whose green state is unreachable gets disabled, so it protects nothing — identical end state to a gate that never goes red.

fact: Upgrading a CLI to fix model errors silently killed every session spawn — two constraints are mutually exclusive across versions.
recommendation: When a version bump 'fixes' one symptom, check what the bump REMOVES. claude <=2.1.120 accepts --sdk-url ws://localhost but 400s on modern models; >=2.1.121 runs modern models but hard-rejects localhost sdk-url (allowlist is compiled in: api/api-staging/api-pr-preview.anthropic.com). No single version satisfies both, so pin-vs-upgrade oscillates forever — change the transport instead.
